Today (Thursday) was a broad green session for Jaleel's book, with 14 of 18 holdings higher, though it remains roughly flat overall at -0.11% unrealized. The rotation out of AI-exposed names into established cash-flow businesses helped the defensives and quality names: ADBE +6.07%, AOS +4.73%, AZO +3.61%, BSX +3.37%, ZTS +2.99%. The pain was in semis. NVDA fell 4.4% and AVGO 4.31% on Fed-hike expectations and capex worries. RKLB fell 4.56%.

The drift is in the names where price and thesis disagree. LULU jumped 7.8%, but the only headline is a "whale activity" note. Its guidance cut, a fifth straight quarter of falling Americas comps and tariff-hit margins are unchanged, and the stock is still -18.6% for Jaleel. RKLB is the worst divergence: -34.6%, an AVOID verdict and a QARP of 36.6 at a 5.5% weight. Together, the two AVOID names are 9.5% of the book. ADBE's rally is rotation, not a resolution of the AI-moat fear. BSX is rated STRONG BUY (QARP 79.0) while management guides flat through Q3.

Watch BSX earnings on Oct 28, the NVDA export-control and AI-capex picture ahead of Nov 17, and the pharma pricing overhang on NVS, NBIX and VRTX.
